headline: Sydney Factory Roof Plants Cool Solar Panels and Boost Output
meta_description: A Sydney factory roof combines 319 solar panels with 14,000 native plants, boosting summer electricity production by 11.1% while keeping panels 28°C cooler.
summary_short: Native plants growing alongside solar panels in Sydney are making the system work harder and cooler—a clever blend of nature and renewable energy.
body:
A Sydney factory has created an unlikely partnership: 319 solar panels sharing roof space with 14,000 native plants. The result is measurable and striking. During summer, the living roof helps the panels produce 11.1% more electricity than they would alone. The plants also keep the panels running at temperatures up to 28°C cooler.

The cooling effect matters more than it might seem at first. Solar panels lose efficiency as they heat up, so bringing down their operating temperature directly translates to better power generation—exactly what the data shows. The addition of native plants creates a secondary benefit: the living roof captures and retains water, reducing runoff while supporting local ecology.

This Sydney installation demonstrates a growing insight: sometimes the best technological solutions aren't purely technological. By integrating nature into industrial infrastructure, designers can solve multiple problems at once—energy production, temperature management, and habitat support—all on the same patch of roof.
quick_facts: Sydney factory roof hosts 319 solar panels and 14,000 native plants
Living roof boosts summer electricity output by 11.1%
Plants keep solar panels running 28°C cooler than without vegetation
